![NLA schematic: the activation verbalizer turns a target activation into a text description, and the activation reconstructor recovers the activation from the text alone. [Watch on YouTube](https://youtu.be/j2knrqAzYVY)](cover.jpg){fig-align="center" data-lightbox-src="cover-full.jpg"}

[Anthropic's](https://www.anthropic.com/) interpretability team [introduces](https://www.anthropic.com/research/natural-language-autoencoders) Natural Language Autoencoders (NLAs), a method for turning an internal activation of a language model into a plain-text explanation. Two copies of the target model are trained jointly: an *activation verbalizer* that reads an activation and writes a text explanation, and an *activation reconstructor* that reads the explanation and rebuilds the activation. The training signal is reconstruction similarity, so explanations that carry real content about the activation are rewarded over explanations that do not. The companion paper on Transformer Circuits [[1]](#ref-1) comes with an interactive demo on [Neuronpedia](http://neuronpedia.org/nla) and training code on [GitHub](https://github.com/kitft/natural_language_autoencoders).

## Methods

![The NLA training loop: the activation verbalizer (AV) translates a target activation $h_{L,i}$ into a natural-language description, and the activation reconstructor (AR) recovers an activation $\hat{h}_{L,i}$ from that text alone. Training minimizes $\|h_{L,i} - \hat{h}_{L,i}\|_2^2$, so descriptions that carry real content about the activation are rewarded. Schematic from the paper's [training section](https://transformer-circuits.pub/2026/nla/index.html#nla-training) [[1]](#ref-1).](figure1.webp){fig-align="center" data-lightbox-src="figure1-full.png"}

## Results

The post applies NLAs to two problems: evaluation awareness and alignment auditing. On a test of destructive coding actions (e.g. deleting important files), NLA explanations flag evaluation awareness 16% of the time in cases where Claude never verbalizes it; on [SWE-bench Verified](https://www.swebench.com/) the rate is 26%; on real [claude.ai](https://claude.ai/) traffic from users who opted in to training it sits under 1%. Anthropic reports that NLAs were used in the pre-deployment alignment audits of Claude Mythos Preview and Claude Opus 4.6.

![Opus 4.6 shows NLA-measured evaluation awareness on 26% of SWE-bench Verified transcripts and 16% of destructive-coding transcripts, versus 1% and 0% when measured by what the model actually verbalizes. On opt-in real claude.ai traffic the NLA-measured rate is 0.4%. Chart from the paper [[1]](#ref-1).](figure2-eval-awareness.webp){fig-align="center" data-lightbox-src="figure2-eval-awareness-full.png"}

In a toy auditing game where a target model has been trained with a single hidden misaligned motivation, auditors equipped with NLAs uncover the motivation 12–15% of the time, compared with 3% or below when given other interpretability tools.

![Auditing-game win rates across tool configs. NLA+conversation auditors identify the target model's misaligned motivation 12/100 without access to training data and 15/100 with access, well above the SAE+conversation (3/100) and conversation-only (1–2/100) baselines. Chart from the paper [[1]](#ref-1).](figure3-auditing.webp){fig-align="center" data-lightbox-src="figure3-auditing-full.png"}

## My Notes

- **NLAs trade mechanistic grounding for direct legibility.** [Sparse autoencoders](https://transformer-circuits.pub/2023/monosemantic-features) (SAE) and [attribution graphs](https://transformer-circuits.pub/2025/attribution-graphs/biology.html) share the autoencoder structure (round-trip reconstruction as the training signal, structured output a trained researcher reads); NLAs swap the sparse feature dictionary for a text bottleneck and the linear readout for another copy of the model. The closest prior art is Patchscope [[2]](#ref-2), which uses a frozen LLM to decode hidden states into natural language without a round-trip training objective. NLAs add the reconstruction loop to tighten what the verbalizer has to say. The paper itself flags the cost as a limitation: an SAE feature is a specific direction in activation space you can causally intervene on, while an NLA explanation is a black-box output of another LLM. That makes NLAs a natural complement to the structural methods rather than a replacement: the SAE or attribution graph tells you *where* in the network a representation lives, and the NLA tells you, in prose, *what it seems to be about*.

- **NLAs move the describing job from the model to a dedicated pair.** The evaluation-awareness numbers tighten a gap that [SelfReflect](/posts/20260430-selfreflect-internal-distribution/) articulated: current LLMs cannot faithfully describe their internal distributions when asked to. NLAs sidestep the asking by training a separate model to do the describing from the activation directly. Where SelfReflect measures a given model's introspective faithfulness as a property of that model, NLAs make reconstruction fidelity the explicit training target, at the cost of training and running a dedicated pair of models for the task. The paper's own caveat — that the training objective "does not explicitly incentivize NLA explanations to be interpretable or faithful" — is why they still have to evaluate faithfulness empirically rather than claim it by construction.

- **Where did the eval-awareness come from in the first place?** Nobody explicitly trained Claude to notice "this is a test", so the signal had to seep in from the training data. Prior work on situational awareness by Berglund et al. [[3]](#ref-3), and its follow-up benchmark by Laine et al. [[4]](#ref-4), has already speculated on the supervision sources: the AI safety literature itself, published openly and full of discussions of evaluation protocols, sandbagging, and red-teaming; benchmark format exposure during pretraining, since SWE-bench-style task-description conventions live on the public web and there is no way to scrub them without hurting capability training; and a structural tell during RLHF, where human raters treating contrived prompts and conversational prompts as different kinds of "good response" teaches the model a distribution over what eval-shaped inputs look like. What none of the prior work has done — and what NLAs now make possible — is a systematic training-data audit: read activations for eval-awareness signals, trace the candidate text sources through the training corpus, and publish the map. That would be the natural companion piece.

- **NLA-measured eval-awareness has a Goodhart half-life.** Frontier models may behave differently during evaluation than during deployment, and NLAs put a number on it. On SWE-bench Verified, activations register "this is a test" on 26% of problems; on opt-in claude.ai traffic, the rate is 0.4%. If that gap holds up under independent interpretability methods, benchmark scores reflect how a frontier model behaves under observation. How it behaves when nobody is watching is a separate question, and the verbalized rate (1% on SWE-bench) tells us the model will not answer it for us. There is a further catch: 26% itself depends on a model that doesn't yet know its activations will be read. Once NLA-style signals enter RLHF or alignment training — and Anthropic is already running NLAs in pre-deployment audits, which is the shortest possible path into that loop — a future model can learn to suppress activation-level eval-awareness without the underlying awareness decreasing. This is the [observer effect](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Observer_effect_(physics)) entering interpretability, with [Goodhart's Law](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goodhart%27s_law) as the stricter limit: measuring the model disturbs it once the measurement loops back into training, and at that point the measure stops tracking what it was measuring. The dynamic has been predicted in theory [[5]](#ref-5) and recently demonstrated empirically in reward-gaming experiments [[6]](#ref-6); what's missing is the direct test on interpretability tools: train on NLA-derived signals, measure NLA quality decay. That would put a half-life on numbers like 26%.

- [Improving Metacognition and Uncertainty Communication in Language Models](/posts/20260525-metacognition-uncertainty-sft/): another route to the same problem, training a model to verbalize its internal confidence rather than reading the activation from the outside.
- [The Anthropic Institute's Research Agenda](/posts/20260516-anthropic-institute-agenda/): the same lab's broader program, of which interpretability tools like NLAs are the technical underpinning for auditing AI systems in the wild.
